documents.title: Pilot Program: HMC AI-Use Course Policies (DRAFT)
documents.stance_why: The draft is a menu of four levels ("four different suggested levels of allowed AI usage") and says "Faculty are not obligated to use these policies", so it sets no stance of its own and offers tiers; stance is delegates.
tiers: Level 0: No AI Use Allowed as it Inhibits Learning
documents.summary: A pilot, non-binding syllabus framework from HMC faculty giving four levels of allowed AI use, from none to open, with sample syllabus text and four constants (Honor Code, acknowledgement, verification, ethics). It also gives instructor tips to reduce incentives for misuse.

units.why: The framework states its aim: "increase clarity for students about what AI usages are allowed or disallowed", an institution-level purpose statement, so P56 (framework preamble), informs/general.
units.anchor: increase clarity for students about what AI usages are allowed or disallowed

units.why: "Faculty are not obligated to use these policies and can modify them" leaves the choice to each instructor, so P04 (instructor decides), actor instructor, phase before-course, modality may.
units.anchor: Faculty are not obligated to use these policies and can modify them

units.why: The document "focuses on usages, as opposed to specific tools (ChatGPT, Gemini, etc)", which sets the scope of what the framework covers; P61 scope definition rather than P05 because it concerns scope, not tiers.
units.anchor: focuses on usages, as opposed to specific tools

units.why: The guide offers "four different suggested levels of allowed AI usage, ranging from most to least permissive", i.e. named tiers, so P05; document stance is delegates.
units.anchor: four different suggested levels of allowed AI usage

units.why: Instructors may apply a level "to all student work for your course, or to individual assignments", a per-course or per-assignment choice, so P04 (not P05, since the point is who and what scope decides).
units.anchor: apply to all student work for your course, or to individual assignments

units.why: Instructors with their own policy should "use a different label (other than AI Use Level 0, 1, 2, or 3)" so labels keep one meaning; this concerns the naming of tiers, so P05.
units.anchor: please use a different label (other than AI Use Level 0, 1, 2, or 3)
units.frag_end: your policy with one of these.

units.why: The suggested syllabus language is "For this course, our policy is [PASTE POLICY HERE]", encouraging instructors to put the chosen level in the syllabus; P09 syllabus statement, should.
units.anchor: For this course, our policy is [PASTE POLICY HERE].

units.why: "HMC students are responsible for upholding the Honor Code, which applies to appropriate use of AI tools" ties AI misuse to the Honor Code; P36 misconduct, student, must.
units.anchor: upholding the Honor Code, which applies to appropriate use of AI tools.

units.why: "Being unsure about something doesn’t excuse a violation" and students should "ask your instructor for clarification first"; P10 ask before using, should.
units.anchor: ask your instructor for clarification first

units.why: "Inadvertent use should also be reported" asks students to self-report accidental use; closest is P38 self-report, should.
units.anchor: Inadvertent use should also be reported.

units.why: "one should always acknowledge when and how AI tools are used in our work" is a disclosure requirement; P24 (the tool name part is coded separately as P25).
units.anchor: one should always acknowledge when and how AI tools are used

units.why: The acknowledgement should include "the specific version and name of the AI tool", a citation detail, so P25 rather than P24.
units.anchor: along with the specific version and name of the AI tool

units.why: "it may also be appropriate to show the exact prompt that you used and the AI’s full, unedited response" is a conditional, softer citation detail (prompt and output); P25, modality may.
units.anchor: show the exact prompt that you used

units.why: "Submitting work as if it were your own without proper acknowledgement of your sources is plagiarism" classes undisclosed AI use as plagiarism; P36.
units.anchor: without proper acknowledgement of your sources is plagiarism.

units.why: "Generative AI tools aren’t reliable sources of information so you should find ways to verify your work" tells students to verify output; P31.
units.anchor: so you should find ways to verify your work

units.why: "Consider the ethical and environmental impacts of using generative AI tools" names ethics and environmental cost; P53, should.
units.anchor: Consider the ethical and environmental impacts of using generative AI tools.

units.why: "Before uploading something to a generative AI tool, do you have permission to do so?" asks students to check permission before uploading material; P49 (course materials/protected works), should.
units.anchor: do you have permission to do so?

units.why: Students should "consider whether generative AI tools might really be the most appropriate tool given your own goals"; this nudges reflection on whether to use AI at all, which fits no listed type (P03 requires discouragement).
units.anchor: consider whether generative AI tools might really be the most appropriate tool
units.uncovered_note: Students should reflect on whether AI is the most appropriate tool for their goals before using it.

units.why: Tip: "Normalize struggle while learning and provide as many options as possible for students to get help", aimed at reducing AI incentive; no type covers instructor-provided help to reduce misuse incentives, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Normalize struggle while learning and provide as many options as possible
units.uncovered_note: Instructors reduce students' incentive to misuse AI by normalizing struggle and offering many routes to help.

units.why: Tip: "avoid all-or-nothing grading in favor of assigning partial credit", a grading redesign to lessen AI incentive; P35.
units.anchor: avoid all-or-nothing grading in favor of assigning partial credit

units.why: Tip: "Periodically remind students about the policy", a communication practice; P09 is the nearest communicate-theme type.
units.anchor: Periodically remind students about the policy

units.why: Tip: "Be transparent about the ways that you use generative AI tools (or not)" asks instructors to disclose their own AI use to students; P47.
units.anchor: Be transparent about the ways that you use generative AI tools

units.why: Tip: "tell students what tools/resources are reliable sources of information" gives alternatives to unreliable AI; no type fits instructor-recommended alternatives, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: tell students what tools/resources are reliable sources of information
units.uncovered_note: Instructors tell students which tools or resources are reliable alternatives to unreliable AI tools.

units.why: Level 0 goal is "to encourage students to develop their own understanding of and fluency with course material", the learning rationale for a ban; P41.
units.anchor: develop their own understanding of and fluency with course material
units.frag_start: The goal of this policy is

units.why: "the use of any generative AI tools is not allowed in this course" is a blanket ban, including brainstorming, source finding, summarizing, code snippets and revision; P01.
units.anchor: the use of any generative AI tools is not allowed in this course
units.policy: At Level 0 the use of any generative AI tools is not allowed in the course, including brainstorming ideas, finding source materials, summarizing ideas, generating code snippets, images or videos, revising writing, or checking work.

units.why: Level 0 use "will be considered a violation of the HMC Honor Code"; P36 misconduct.
units.anchor: will be considered a violation of the HMC Honor Code

units.why: Disallowed uses include "generate code snippets, images, or videos", which is AI producing submitted work; P19.
units.anchor: generate code snippets, images, or videos
units.policy: At Level 0 students may not use generative AI tools to generate code snippets, images, or videos.

units.why: Disallowed uses also include "revise your writing, or check your work"; P21 (proofread or check graded work).
units.anchor: revise your writing, or check your work
units.policy: At Level 0 students may not use generative AI tools to revise their writing or check their work.

units.why: "Tools that automatically flag spelling and grammatical errors as you write are allowed, but not tools that offer suggested revisions" separates acceptable proofing from AI prose revision; P18.
units.anchor: Tools that automatically flag spelling and grammatical errors as you write are allowed

units.why: "If English is not your first language, please ask me about whether tools for translating" routes translation questions to the instructor; P18 (translation tools).
units.anchor: please ask me about whether tools for translating words or texts between languages are allowed

units.why: Level 1 describes "outsourcing tasks that you already know how to do well, or tasks that aren’t the primary focus" as acceptable time saving; this defines a tier (P05).
units.anchor: outsourcing tasks that you already know how to do well

units.why: Allowed example: "writing code to automate an ancillary task for an assignment" in a language the student is fluent in, a narrow allowed code use; P16.
units.anchor: writing code to automate an ancillary task for an assignment

units.why: Allowed example: "checking whether your bibliography is consistently formatted" is prose-side tool use; P18.
units.anchor: checking whether your bibliography is consistently formatted using the right bibliographic style

units.why: Allowed example: "checking your writing for spelling or grammatical errors" is prose support; P18.
units.anchor: checking your writing for spelling or grammatical errors

units.why: The calculator comparison and the warning "AI is not analogous to a calculator" because outputs vary and are opaque is a reliability point; P31.
units.anchor: AI is not analogous to a calculator

units.why: At Level 1 AI is "not permitted for" "chatting with an AI chatbot to get answers to conceptual questions about course content", a ban on the tutor use; P12 because that is the topic, with unit_stance prohibit.
units.anchor: chatting with an AI chatbot to get answers to conceptual questions about course content

units.policy: At Level 1 generative AI tools are not permitted for chatting with an AI chatbot to get answers to conceptual questions about course content.

units.frag_end: brainstorming ideas for a research paper;
units.policy: At Level 1 generative AI tools are not permitted for brainstorming ideas for a research paper.

units.why: At Level 1 AI is not permitted for "major revisions for a paper"; prose rule, P18.
units.anchor: major revisions for a paper
units.frag_start: In this class, generative AI tools
units.policy: At Level 1 generative AI tools are not permitted for major revisions for a paper.

units.why: "Please ask me if you have any questions about whether a specific usage is allowed or not" repeats ask-first guidance at Level 1; P10.
units.anchor: Please ask me if you have any questions about whether a specific usage is allowed

units.why: Level 2 goal is use "while retaining intellectual ownership and primary effort of their work", so students stay the primary problem-solver; P32.
units.anchor: retaining intellectual ownership and primary effort of their work
units.frag_start: The goal of this policy is to allow students to use generative AI tools in their learning while
units.frag_end: form of your work needs to be the result of your own effort.

units.why: Level 2 permits "brainstorming alternatives or options for an idea that you’ve developed yourself"; P15.
units.anchor: brainstorming alternatives or options for an idea that you’ve developed yourself

units.why: Level 2 permits "seeking alternative explanations for course content" and "chatting with an AI chatbot to get answers to conceptual questions"; tutor use, P12.
units.anchor: seeking alternative explanations for course content to help you understand the material

units.why: Level 2 permits "revising writing to improve clarity, grammar, or style but not to alter your own ideas"; P18.
units.anchor: revising writing to improve clarity, grammar, or style but not to alter your own ideas

units.frag_end: fix those errors on your own.

units.anchor: you no longer can claim primary intellectual ownership of the work

documents.title: AI and Students
documents.stance_why: The page says students "must consult with the instructor and course policies" and that guidelines "complement—not replace—the specific instructions" of faculty, setting no rule itself; stance is delegates.
documents.summary: A short Computing and Information Services page telling students to follow each instructor's AI policy, to prefer college-licensed AI tools (Gemini, NotebookLM, Copilot) for data protection, and to respect copyright and the Honor Code.

units.why: "Students must consult with the instructor and course policies – seeking clarification as needed – before using AI for academic work": ask first, P10.
units.anchor: Students must consult with the instructor and course policies
units.frag_end: before using AI for academic work.

units.why: "Students should make sure they understand AI guidelines for their classes and other academic projects (e.g. Clinic, thesis)": the rule is set per course or project, so P11.
units.anchor: make sure they understand AI guidelines for their classes and other academic projects

units.why: "The operational guidelines referenced on this site are intended to complement—not replace—the specific instructions and expectations set by individual faculty members" delegates to instructors; P04.
units.anchor: complement—not replace—the specific instructions and expectations set by individual faculty members

units.why: "students should make sure they are familiar with which AI Use policy is in place for the class", pointing to the faculty levels; P05.
units.anchor: which AI Use policy is in place for the class in question

units.why: "students have access to AI that meets college data protection requirements" (Gemini, NotebookLM, Copilot): college-provided tools, P17.
units.anchor: students have access to AI that meets college data protection requirements for AI tools

units.why: "they are strongly encouraged to use these tools as opposed to consumer versions" prefers vetted tools; P50.
units.anchor: they are strongly encouraged to use these tools as opposed to consumer versions

units.why: "ensures that your data is private and is not used to train large language models" explains the privacy benefit of college tools; P50.
units.anchor: ensures that your data is private and is not used to train large language models

units.why: "it is really important to understand how the college classifies data and how that affects which AI tools can be used" is a data-protection duty; P50.
units.anchor: understand how the college classifies data and how that affects which AI tools

units.why: "Be mindful of copyright and whether you have permission to use other people’s content (eg course materials or another student’s work)": permission before putting course materials into AI, P49.
units.anchor: whether you have permission to use other people’s content

units.why: "Please keep your obligations under the honor code in mind" links AI use to the Honor Code; P36.
units.anchor: Please keep your obligations under the honor code in mind.

notes: Coder A. Level-based bans or permissions on tutor and brainstorming uses were typed by topic (P12, P15) with unit_stance prohibit. Three UNCOVERED units: instructor tips on reducing misuse incentives and reliable alternatives, and student reflection on whether AI is the appropriate tool.
